Hello, by visiting this subverse I imagine you are a either A) A slinger yourself B) Looking for a cheap and fun hobby C) Curious as to what this is all about.

What are slings?

Slings are very ancient weapons that are noted for there power and simplicity. They consist of a piece of cordage (string, leather etc.) with a knot at one end, a loop at the other end, and a pouch in the middle. The idea is that a stone is placed in the middle of the sling, with a finger/hand/wrist in the loop. The knot on the other end placed between the thumb and forefinger. The sling is spun to gain momentum and at just the right moment the knot is released causing the pouch to launch the projectile forward.

Its just a stupid piece of rope, how powerful could it be?

The power of these weapons is not to be underestimated. Many are familiar with the story of David and Goliath. Using just a sling David killed a heavily armored man over 9ft tall! Historians like Herodotus write about the effectiveness of slingers in the armies of antiquity. Sling bullets were attested to having impeccable range (ancient writers repeatedly stress the great range of slings) and deadly concussive force against armored foes. In the mid-east Assyrian reliefs depict slingers effectively used in conquest. While in the Americas it is attested that Incan slingers were still a formidable threat to Spanish conquerors even though they themselves had firearms.

Ok they may be powerful but is it really that fun of a hobby?

Yes! Slinging and better yet making slings is an excellent low cost hobby. Unlike guns and bows, the sling is simple and cheap to make and is easy to find ammunition for. There are many techniques that I will share (If there is interest) on how to make and use simple to complex slings that you can use for your own practice. There is something almost therapeutic about hearing the snap of a sling and the whistling twang of a launched projectile.

Even if this does interest me, are there that many other people who share this interest?

Sadly the slinging community is much smaller than the archery or firearm community. It might be hard to find anyone who slings anywhere near where you live. However, archery itself was a sport that was in decline for sometime until a revival in the 19th and 20th centuries, with even more interest garnered with recent movies. Hopefully with help from other slinging enthusiasts we can show on this subverse how fun this hobby really is. I'll try to post as much content as I can with the ultimate goal to spread awareness about how awesome it is to sling.

Enjoy!
